title: keyval.observation/v1
description: One simulation run's observations: what the clients and the harness saw, independently of what the system claims. The oracles (the reference model and checkers K-1 to K-12, plus non-vacuity, K-13) read only this, never production types (T-12, PLAN.md §10.2, §10.5). See schemas/observation/README.md for the stream rules and which checker reads which record.

voters.description: The configured voters: one, three or five (§7.10).

complete.description: False when a required observation overflowed its bound, the event budget ran out or the scenario was invalid: the run is incomplete, which fails (P10, §10.16).

event_budget.description: Scheduler events used against the manifest's `max_events` (§10.16: the budget must not be exhausted).

scenario.description: Whether the scenario kept the healthy envelope's bounds (§9.4). An invalid scenario is reported, names the bound it broke, and makes the run incomplete (§10.16): a generator defect, not a liveness failure.

attempt_id.description: An attempt, numbered within the run; unique per `invoke`.

digest.description: A SHA-256 digest as 64 lowercase hex characters.

hex_bytes.description: Bytes as lowercase hex (at most the 66 KiB canonical-command limit, §7.11).

key.description: A key (DM-1: 1 to 256 bytes of UTF-8; consumers measure bytes after decoding).

value.description: A value (DM-2: 0 to 65,536 bytes of UTF-8).

write_operation.description: A write, in the API's terms (§8.2).

operation.description: What the attempt asked for, in the API's terms (§8.2). A SCAN's null `limit` means the default page of 32 items (§7.11).

command.description: A committed entry's command: its request ID and write.

served_by.description: Which node answered, and the applied prefix it answered from (F-2, C-3).

write_outcome.description: A write's response (§8.1, §8.4): `ok` for a 200, otherwise the error code. Per code exactly the fields §8.4 lists are non-null; the constant or derivable ones (`message`, `guidance`, `nodes`) are left out.

terminal_result.description: A stored terminal result, as a status lookup returns it (F-9, §8.3): the body a same-ID retry would receive now, so `replayed` is true. `request_id_conflict` is never stored.

scan_outcome.description: A SCAN page or refusal (§8.2, §8.5). When `has_more` is true, `next_after` is the last returned key; otherwise it is null.

status_outcome.description: A status lookup's response (F-9): `known` with the stored terminal result, or `unknown` as of `served_by` (never a claim of absence).

hard_state.description: A Raft hard state's durable part: term and vote (DUR-2).

obligation.description: What a release depends on (DUR-2): the hard state, when it carries one, and the node's log up to `last_index`, whose entry has term `last_term` (0 for an empty prefix).

durable_state.description: Durable Raft state (DUR-2): term, vote, and the log up to `last_index`, whose entry has term `last_term` (0 for an empty log), so a sync before a suffix replacement never covers the replacement.

overflow.description: A required observation that overflowed its bound (§7.11): the run is incomplete and fails (P10).

limits.description: The semantic limits the reference model needs (§7.10; small test limits in capacity profiles, §10.3).

manifest.description: The run manifest (§10.2), the swarm's fault selection (§10.4), how the heal completes, the tick length that converts tick budgets to `time`, and the semantic limits.

heal.description: How the heal completes (§10.2): a catch-up marker; a marker key pre-created during baseline (DM-6 profiles); or a certified drain with no marker (DM-7 profiles).

record_phase.description: A run phase begins (§10.2 run phases): setup, baseline, chaos, heal and check, each once and in that order. Non-vacuity (§10.16) reads successful writes before the first fault and after heal against these.

record_fault.description: The nemesis started or ended a fault (§9.1, §10.4): a crash and its restart, a partition and its healing, a stall and its resumption. A permanent loss only starts. A crash names, per crashed node, where in its disk work it struck.

nodes.description: The nodes it affects; empty for a fault on links only.

record_invoke.description: A simulated client invoked an operation: one attempt, one request to one node incarnation (the node's current one when the request is sent, even when it is down and the request is lost). A logical write is all the attempts sharing a request ID, misuse attempts excluded (§10.3). Recorded by the client, independently of anything the system claims. Simulated clients drive the core with parsed domain requests (§10.2), so `invalid_request` and `too_large` outcomes are representable for completeness only.

misuse.description: True for the misuse stream's reuse of a request ID with a different command; such attempts are never logical writes (§10.3).

record_attempt.description: A write attempt moved through §7.8's lifecycle on the node handling it: admitted (`NotSubmitted`), answered from the applied history (short circuit), attached to the pending same-ID, same-digest proposal of attempt `attached_to`, submitted (recorded where the proposal is handed to the consensus library, not from the attempt's own bookkeeping), dropped (a synchronous `ProposalDropped` with nothing appended: not submitted after all, A-5), or terminal (an entry carrying its request ID applied). Unknown outcome is not a state: it is a response.

record_response.description: A node incarnation generated the response to an attempt, as the client will see it (§8.2, §8.4). `op` repeats the invoked operation so the outcome's shape can be checked here. `generation` is the incarnation's response-generation order, the order K-6 judges; arrival at the client is a separate `delivery` record.

record_delivery.description: One copy of an attempt's response reached its client, or was lost on the way (§9.1 message loss). Duplication can deliver a response more than once; the first copy delivered is what the client observed first.

record_append.description: An entry was appended to a node incarnation's log (volatile until a sync covers it): its index (one past the log's end), term and exact payload bytes. With `truncate` and `recovered`, these give every node's log after every step (T-5), which K-8 judges.

record_truncate.description: A node incarnation removed its log suffix from `from_index` on (a conflicting suffix replaced, §7.6).

record_recovered.description: A node incarnation began: what it recovered from its disk (§7.7, §9.1 crash-restart), before it takes any other step. `log` is its whole recovered log and `durable` its durable state; incarnation 0 starts empty.

record_sync.description: A durability obligation (DUR-2) was requested, completed, or its completion delivered stale to a later incarnation, which must ignore it (B-17). `covers` is what the sync makes durable: the term, the vote and the log as it was when the sync was requested, up to `last_index` (never the commit index).

record_accept.description: A replica incarnation accepted the entry at `index` while in `acceptance_term`: a follower when it acknowledges the entry, the leader when its own sync covering the entry completes; K-11 judges that the entry was durable there first (K-8's commit certificates: an entry of term T is committed once a majority accepted it from the term-T leader during term T). `payload_digest` is SHA-256 of the entry's payload bytes, so two different entries at one index never merge into one certificate.

record_release.description: A node released something that depends on durable state (K-11): a vote grant, an append acknowledgement, a client success (a response carrying a terminal execution decision: a write's `ok`, `version_mismatch` or `capacity_exceeded`) or a published read (a read answered with `served_by`). The last two name the `attempt` they answer. `requires` is the DUR-2 obligation, derived by the harness from the outgoing message, not claimed by the node: a vote grant needs the term and vote it carries (its `last_index` is 0); an append acknowledgement needs those and the log up to the acknowledged index; a client success or published read needs the log up to the decided or served index, never a term or vote sync (F-7). A pre-vote grant persists nothing and is not a release.

record_committed.description: An entry became committed: the harness records it once a commit certificate forms from the `accept` records, for it or for a later index whose certifiers hold it (K-8: a certified entry and the prefix before it; K-8 recomputes this). `payload` is the entry's exact bytes, empty for an empty (no-op) entry; `command` is the harness's decoding of them, null exactly for an empty entry. The reference model replays `command`s, which is how first executions and their results are derived (§10.14), never taken from a node's claim.

record_node_state.description: A node's god-view state after a step in which it changed (T-5), recorded at the point of the change, before any later record of that step. It holds until that node's next `node_state`, so these records give every node's state after every step. On a crash the process is `crashed` and the rest is the state it last had.

record_marker.description: A node applied the catch-up marker (§10.2 heal). Its state digest at that application is what K-7 compares.

record_lost.description: The permanent-loss set changed: the nodes removed for good so far (§9.1, at most two). K-1, K-7, K-9 and K-13 exclude them.

record_quiescence.description: All client activity stopped: no client request queued or in flight on any node (§10.2 heal, K-9, K-12). Only status lookups follow it.

record_drain.description: A certified drain held over the quiet period (§10.2, `drain` heal): a stable current-term leader, and on every recoverable node last log index = commit index = applied index with identical state digests.

record_resolution.description: How the run resolved a logical write (§10.2, §9.3), once per logical write after its last attempt: executed at `index`, not executed (`unknown` on every recoverable node after a certified drain), refused (`history_full` with no submitted attempt), or unresolved (a liveness failure, K-9). `evidence` names the attempts whose responses decide it.
